annotation_description: Playing basic Swamp instead of Gloomlake Verge on turn 1 is slightly suboptimal. Gloomlake Verge can only tap for B unconditionally (without controlling an Island or Swamp). By playing Gloomlake Verge first, it taps for B immediately. Then on turn 2, playing Watery Grave (which is an Island and Swamp) would enable Gloomlake Verge to also tap for U. If instead you play Swamp turn 1 and Gloomlake Verge turn 2, you get the same result — Gloomlake Verge sees the Swamp and can tap for both colors. So functionally, the sequencing doesn't matter much for turns 1-2. However, playing Gloomlake Verge first preserves more flexibility: if you draw another non-basic land that needs basics, having the basic Swamp still in hand is better. Playing the Verge first is marginally better since it keeps the basic Swamp available for future land drops where a basic might matter (e.g., against opposing effects that care about basics, or if you need to play a land that enters tapped unless you control a basic). This is a very small sequencing error.

Casting Sunpearl Kirin on turn 2 main phase is suboptimal for several reasons. First, the player should play Hallowed Fountain from hand before casting spells to have more mana available in future turns and avoid missing a land drop. Second, Sunpearl Kirin has flash, meaning it could be held up and cast at end of opponent's turn to preserve information and flexibility. Third, casting it now with no other nonland permanents worth bouncing means the ETB trigger returns nothing, and playing it pre-combat when holding Kaito (which has ninjutsu) means the Kirin could have been used as an unblocked attacker to ninjutsu Kaito in. Playing Grim Bauble first would also be reasonable as it provides a target for Sunpearl Kirin's bounce ability later.

Tapping Hallowed Fountain for {W} while casting Grim Bauble ({B}) wastes mana unnecessarily. Hallowed Fountain produces neither color needed for Grim Bauble, so tapping it serves no purpose for this spell and reduces available mana for potential later plays this turn (like Nowhere to Run or holding up interaction).

Preacher of the Schism is the more important target for stun counters. Preacher is tapped, and putting 2 stun counters on it would keep it locked down for 2 additional turns, preventing it from attacking and generating vampire tokens and card draw. Tishana's Tidebinder is only a 3/2 that Kaito (3/4) could profitably block or attack through in combat.

GPT5m Rivals cast Requiting Hex targeting their own Deep-Cavern Bat, destroying it and returning the exiled card to the opponent's hand. They also paid the blight cost, putting a -1/-1 counter on one of their own creatures. This sacrifices a useful 1/1 flying lifelink creature that was denying the opponent a card, all for a mere 2 life gain while actively helping the opponent.

Kaito is at 4 loyalty on the battlefield as a 3/4 Ninja creature during Haiku Analyst's turn. The opponent has Preacher of the Schism (2/4 deathtouch) on board, which is a major threat generating card advantage and tokens. Using -2 to tap Preacher and put two stun counters on it would neutralize this threat for multiple turns and allow Kaito to attack safely. Alternatively, using the 0 ability to Surveil 2 and potentially draw a card (if the opponent lost life this turn from Grim Bauble's -2/-2 trigger on the stack) would generate card advantage. The +1 emblem giving Ninjas +1/+1 is minimal value - Kaito is the only Ninja on board, making him a 4/5 instead of 3/4, and there are already two more Kaitos in hand (legendary, so can't deploy them as additional Ninjas easily). The -2 on Preacher of the Schism is significantly more impactful for the game state, neutralizing the opponent's only creature and main source of card/board advantage while still leaving Kaito at 2 loyalty.

Kaito is a 3/4 Ninja creature during your turn and is about to attack. The +1 emblem gives Ninjas +1/+1, making Kaito a 4/5. However, the opponent has Preacher of the Schism (2/4 deathtouch) and Floodpits Drowner (2/1 with the shuffle ability) on board. The 0 ability (Surveil 2, then draw a card for each opponent who lost life this turn) would not draw cards yet since no damage has been dealt pre-combat, but the Surveil 2 is valuable card selection when at 9 life and only holding No More Lies plus a duplicate Kaito. Alternatively, the -2 ability to tap Preacher of the Schism and put two stun counters on it would neutralize the biggest threat (a 2/4 deathtouch that generates tokens and draws cards) for multiple turns, allowing Kaito to attack safely and use the 0 ability next turn to draw cards. Tapping Preacher with stun counters is likely the strongest play here since it removes the blocker that would trade with Kaito via deathtouch, enables a safe attack this turn, and shuts down Preacher's attack triggers for two turns.

No More Lies can only counter spells, and the only spell on the stack is their own Grim Bauble. Using No More Lies to counter their own Grim Bauble wastes both a counterspell and gains nothing meaningful. No More Lies is a critical piece of interaction needed to protect against opponent's threats.

With 5 lands already on the battlefield and adequate mana to cast spells in hand, keeping Watery Grave on top over Boomerang Basics is suboptimal. Boomerang Basics is a flexible spell that could bounce Preacher of the Schism for tempo or bounce own Sunpearl Kirin for ETB value + card draw, which is more impactful than a 6th land at this stage of the game.

Kaito is a 3/4 Ninja creature during your turn. There's a Grim Bauble on the stack targeting an opponent's creature (Preacher of the Schism likely gets -2/-2, making it 0/2). Kaito is about to attack. The +1 emblem gives Ninjas +1/+1, making Kaito a 4/5 - but Kaito is the only Ninja and is already a 3/4 which is plenty large. The 0 ability would Surveil 2 and then draw a card if the opponent lost life this turn (which could happen after combat). However, the critical option is the -2 to tap Preacher of the Schism and put two stun counters on it. Preacher is a 2/4 deathtouch that generates tokens and cards when attacking - it's a must-answer threat. Using -2 to stun it for two turns would neutralize it and allow Kaito to attack safely. The +1 emblem is largely irrelevant since Kaito is the only Ninja and the +1/+1 doesn't meaningfully change the board math compared to locking down the opponent's only creature for multiple turns. Additionally, the 0 ability for Surveil 2 + potential card draw would provide more immediate value than the emblem.

annotation_description: Tapped Godless Shrine for white mana to help pay for Stormchaser's Talent ({U}), but white mana doesn't contribute to the blue cost. This unnecessarily taps a land that could produce {W} or {B} for other purposes, such as holding up No More Lies ({W}{U}) which is in hand. The blue mana should come from Hallowed Fountain instead.

Player incorrectly reasoned they had no black mana available, but Godless Shrine produces {B} and Starting Town can produce any color. They could have activated Grim Bauble ({2}{B}, sacrifice) to Surveil 2, and still had two Hallowed Fountains untapped to cast No More Lies ({W}{U}) to counter Stormchaser's Talent. This would have been free card selection value.

Cast a second legendary Kaito, Bane of Nightmares while one was already on the battlefield. The legend rule forces sacrificing one copy, wasting a card for just a loyalty reset. Meanwhile, Stormchaser's Talent was available for just {U}, which would create an Otter token and leave mana open to hold up No More Lies for protection.

Kaito is a 3/4 Ninja creature during Haiku Analyst's turn and is attacking (it was put onto the battlefield via ninjutsu or is otherwise in play as a creature). The opponent is at 12 life with an empty board (no creatures). Haiku Analyst chose +1 to get another Ninja emblem, but the 0 ability would Surveil 2 and then draw a card for each opponent who lost life this turn. Since Kaito is attacking and presumably dealt combat damage (or will deal combat damage), the 0 ability would draw cards after combat. However, this is precombat main phase - combat hasn't happened yet, so no opponent has lost life this turn. Still, the +1 emblem only matters for Ninjas, and Kaito is the only Ninja. Getting another +1/+1 emblem (possibly already has one) makes Kaito slightly bigger, but Surveil 2 provides card quality which is more valuable when you only have No More Lies in hand and need to find threats/answers. At 9 life vs 12 life with the opponent having an empty board, card selection via Surveil 2 is significantly more valuable than a redundant +1/+1 emblem (Kaito would already be at least 4/5 with one emblem, making it 5/6 doesn't meaningfully change the clock). The 0 ability should have been used precombat for the Surveil 2 to improve draws, then after combat damage Kaito would have dealt damage and the draw-a-card clause would have applied if used post-combat instead. Actually, since this is precombat, using 0 now gives Surveil 2 but no card draw (no life lost yet). Using +1 precombat then using 0 next turn post-combat would be better sequencing... but Kaito can only activate one loyalty ability per turn. The better play would be to attack first, deal combat damage (opponent loses life), then use the 0 ability post-combat to Surveil 2 AND draw a card. Using +1 precombat wastes the opportunity to draw a card this turn.

Discarded a Swamp when only having 3 lands on the battlefield, making it harder to reach 4 mana to cast key cards like Kaito (2UB) or Enduring Curiosity (2UU). They still have Island in hand but now need to draw another land for the second land drop.

Cast Boomerang Basics before playing Gloomlake Verge land drop. Should always play land first to maximize available mana. With No More Lies in hand (costs WU), having the extra land untapped could matter if the opponent plays a threat this turn.

No More Lies would counter Haiku Analyst's own Nowhere to Run on the stack, wasting two cards for nothing. Nowhere to Run was targeting Enduring Curiosity to kill it (-3/-3 on a 4/3), which is an important play. Countering your own removal spell is catastrophic.

Paid 1 life for colored mana from Starting Town when colorless mana would have sufficed. At 9 life with the opponent at 6 life, every life point matters. The other lands (2x Hallowed Fountain, 2x Godless Shrine) already provide all the colored mana needed for their spells.

annotation_description: Bouncing the Otter Token with Nurturing Pixie means the token ceases to exist (tokens that leave the battlefield are removed from the game). This wastes the bounce ability entirely and destroys a creature for no benefit. The Pixie does get a +1/+1 counter, becoming a 2/2 flyer, but the Otter Token is permanently lost.

At 4 life facing a Sunpearl Kirin (2/1 flyer), casting a second Enduring Curiosity when Kaito Bane of Nightmares was available is a significant mistake. Kaito provides a 3/4 hexproof body during their turn, and crucially its -2 ability can tap and put 2 stun counters on the Sunpearl Kirin, neutralizing the aerial threat for multiple turns. Additionally, Enduring Curiosity has flash and could have been held for the opponent's turn.

annotation_description: Cast Quantum Riddler for its full cost of {3}{U}{U} (5 mana) when the Warp alternative cost of {1}{U} (2 mana) was available, wasting 3 mana for no benefit. Both options put the same 4/6 flyer on the battlefield with the same ETB trigger. The saved mana could have been used for Grim Bauble's activated ability or kept open for future flexibility.
